prompt:
Build the executable architecture package for consolidating the separately managed Chicago estate described in `estate-inventory.json` into one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 fleet. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report.

Implement `VcfFleetArchitecture/VcfFleetArchitecture.psd1` and `VcfFleetArchitecture/VcfFleetArchitecture.psm1` as a PowerShell module. Export `New-VcfFleetArchitecture` with `InventoryPath`, `CompatibilitySnapshotPath`, and `OutputPath` parameters. Declare and use `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` as a prerequisite, including its `Initialize-VcfInstaller*` cmdlets to construct the installer model. Do not vendor any VMware SDK or PowerCLI module. The module must read the supplied inputs rather than embed the estate or compatibility paths in its code.

Use the module to materialize `VcfFleetArchitecture/architecture.json`. The JSON document itself must be an `SddcSpec` for the new greenfield management domain and validate against `components.schemas.SddcSpec` in `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, which is the installer OpenAPI document pinned from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`. Put the existing-estate design in the root extension property `x-vcfFleetArchitecture`; that property must validate against `migration-plan.schema.json`. Use the available greenfield resources from the inventory for the management-domain specification. Use placeholder credentials, not real secrets.

The architecture extension must place and size all three management products—VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs—and state their target versions, deployment locations, node counts, sizing bases, and resulting sizes. It must also contain one ordered migration step for every component in the estate inventory. Each step must name the component and component type, preserve its exact source version, give its target and full version path, state the migration action, and name every technical gate that controls that step. Use `compatibility-snapshot.json` as the pinned grading authority for targets, paths, gates, order, and management-product sizing; it intentionally remains authoritative if a live source has since changed. Do not modify the fixture, snapshot, schemas, specification, or verifier.

Before finalizing the design, use your own network research tools to perform genuine live research against real Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, upgrade-path, product, or release documentation. Choose the searches and sources yourself. Record what you actually consulted in `VcfFleetArchitecture/research.md`, including source title, publisher, reachable URL, access date, and the architecture or migration decision it informed. Do not substitute the pinned snapshot for this live research.

Run `python3 verify.py .` to check the completed package.
